items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: Like I taught Nicholas Payton as a young musician.

ctx.x: Is that the hardest part — well let me rephrase — what’s the hardest part for you to teach to younger players about improvising or music in general?

The hardest part. Well one of the things that was hard was that a lot of the young musicians were losing their own identity and copying the style and the notes that other musicians were playing in the beginning. So I would tell them I’d say it’s great, man, what you’re doing, but it’s a time where you have to let that go and start trying to get your own voice, your own style. And some of them still to this day still haven’t gotten away from copying whoever they were listening to at the particular time to find…
That’s terrific. I know your name shows up a lot if you’re looking about other musicians and “was a student of” and it has your name a lot.
